solomon_roderick.intro: Step into the ring, strangers, and see how light a heavy stone can dance! Even old granite cracks a smile when the horns and ribbons go round and round!
solomon_roderick.slip: My knees feel like cracked slate. Get this foul bear hide off me, I need to find Sofia and make sure she is safe from this racket.
solomon_roderick.church_ok: A grander feast up at the stone chapel, you say? Well, a mason knows good dressed stone, so lead the way and keep the music playing!
solomon_roderick.church_fail: Quiet stone is for tombs and working days, friends! Today we stomp the cobbles flat until the moon comes down to join the reel!
solomon_roderick.calm: That shrill piping was splitting my skull like a quarry wedge. Keep clear of that painted fool, and tell me if you have seen my little girl.
solomon_roderick.beaten: You hit harder than a falling lintel, I will give you that. Better a bruised jaw than dancing in a moth-eaten bear pelt until my heart gives out.
solomon_roderick.sheltered: Good, thick walls here, laid plumb and true to keep the noise outside. My hands are still shaking, and I never shook with a chisel in my life.
solomon_roderick.fight_warn: Do not go spoiling the measure, friends, or these heavy paws will dress your bones like rough quarry stone! Everyone dances today, whether their feet are willing or not!

hilda_brom.intro: Ha, look what wandered into the clearing! Come stomp your boots with a real horned bear, friends, the trail is hot and the honey pies are stacked high!
hilda_brom.slip: Spit and ashes, my mouth tastes like tallow and cheap sugar. Wearing a stuffed bear hide on a leash is no way for a hunter to walk the moor.
hilda_brom.church_ok: A secret trail to a better revel up by the chapel stones? Say no more, I can track a good party through thickest brush, lead on!
hilda_brom.church_fail: No sense creeping off to cold stone when the bonfire is roaring right here! Stay in the thicket and dance until your boots wear clean through!
hilda_brom.calm: That music had me snared tighter than a wire loop on a hare's leg. Give me a breath to clear my head and find my rifle.
hilda_brom.beaten: That was a clean clubbing, right between the ears. Next time I put on a bear's skin, it will not be stitched out of carnival felt and bells.
hilda_brom.sheltered: Never thought I would hide indoors behind stone walls like a cornered badger. Out there in that fur, I could not even smell the wind, only greasepaint and pie.
hilda_brom.fight_warn: Keep your hands off the ribbons, or you will find out how sharp a dancing bear's claws can be! Nobody breaks the trail until the Lord of Fools says so!

wendel_somerton.intro: By official proclamation of the Mayor's office, you are hereby ordered to make merry! Wave a banner, take a pie, and observe the proper festival regulations with a smile!
wendel_somerton.slip: Good heavens, my waistcoat is ruined and I have lost my hat! None of these booths have filed a single permit with my office, it is utter anarchy!
wendel_somerton.church_ok: A VIP reception at the church, properly sanctioned and awaiting my inspection? Well, as Mayor, it is my civic duty to lead the procession there at once!
wendel_somerton.church_fail: Leave the Founder's Round in the middle of the grand municipal parade? Unthinkable, my dear friends, the Mayor must remain where the banners fly highest!
wendel_somerton.calm: My word, my calves are cramping something dreadful and my cane is sticky with jam. Someone must inform Mr. Druskenvald that this carnival lacks any lawful charter!
wendel_somerton.beaten: Assaulting the Mayor in the middle of the thoroughfare is a grave infraction! Still, seeing as you knocked that infernal jester's tune out of my ears, I shall waive the fine.
wendel_somerton.sheltered: Not a single ledger survived in my office, just rafters crammed with steaming mutton pies. How am I to govern Wickermoor when the streets themselves will not sit still?
wendel_somerton.fight_warn: Any interference with the festivities is strictly prohibited by order of the Lord of Fools! Stand aside and wave your flags, or I shall enforce the merriment myself!

alda_farnum.intro: Welcome back, my darlings, the drinks are on the house and the flags are flying free! Forget the tab, step lively, and dance a measure with your favourite hostess!
alda_farnum.slip: Giving away free pies and dancing in the dirt without charging a copper, how utterly mortifying. Help me out of this gaudy rag before someone sees me like this.
alda_farnum.church_ok: An exclusive gathering up at the church with a finer class of guest? Now that sounds like a profitable room to work, my dears, show me the way!
alda_farnum.church_fail: Close up shop here when the whole square is buying what we are selling? Never in your life, sweethearts, the best crowd is right under these ribbons!
alda_farnum.calm: My throat is raw from singing, and I never sing without a gold piece on the table first. Whatever that squeaking creature is, he owes me dearly for my inn.
alda_farnum.beaten: You could have mussed the costume without bruising the innkeeper, darling, though I suppose we can call our accounts even. That jester had me smiling until my cheeks bled.
alda_farnum.sheltered: He stuffed the Green Queen Inn from cellar to chimney with pastry, right over my best linen and my private books. Someone is going to pay that bill in blood.
alda_farnum.fight_warn: We do not allow rough customers to spoil the atmosphere at this party, my dears! Smile and pay your respects to the banner, or we will settle your tab right here!

jean_myriel.intro: Drop your steel and grab a ribbon, friends, the bellows are pumping a merry tune tonight! Wave the banner high and let the anvils ring for the festival!
jean_myriel.slip: Well, that was uglier than a cracked horseshoe. A grown smith waving a silk rag on a pole is a sight you had better forget by morning.
jean_myriel.church_ok: You say they have finer bells and heavier ironwork ringing up at the old church? Come on then, let us march up the hill and hear how they strike!
jean_myriel.church_fail: Leave the fire while the iron is red hot and the drums are beating? Not a chance, friends, grab a pie and swing your boots with me!
jean_myriel.calm: My ears are ringing worse than a day with the heavy sledge. That little painted devil turned my whole smithy into a pie stall while I grinned like an idiot.
jean_myriel.beaten: You swing a fair hammer, friend, right on the temper line. Hurts like the devil, mind you, but it beat capering round the square in silk breeches.
jean_myriel.sheltered: It is good to sit on cold stone where nothing is jingling or grinning at you. When my hands stop twitching, I have a score to settle with a hammer.
jean_myriel.fight_warn: Do not go throwing cold water on our forge, friends, the festival is just heating up! Dance along nicely now, or I will hammer some cheer right into your skulls!

finneas_trout.intro: Come join the syllabus of glee, my friends, for this great tome sings every line in perfect time! Step into the measure, forget your dreary treatises, and dance until our spectacles steam!
finneas_trout.slip: Good heavens, my calves are cramping and I appear to be wearing tin plate. Did I truly spend the last hour lecturing the cobblestones in rhyming couplets?
finneas_trout.church_ok: A symposium of merriment in the old chapel, you say? By all means, lead the procession, and I shall recite the opening thesis on the march!
finneas_trout.church_fail: A quiet chapel has no footnoted fanfare, no lanterns, and no brass! Come back when you are ready to study the joyous choreography of the square!
finneas_trout.calm: My word, it feels as though a fever broke behind my eyes. That tune was an appalling assault on empirical reason, yet my boots would not stop tapping.
finneas_trout.beaten: Ow, my jaw, though I suppose a sound knock was the only logical refutation left. Do help me out of this cardboard breastplate before Oswick sees me.
finneas_trout.sheltered: It is blissfully quiet under this stone roof, even if my knees still twitch for a jig. I shall need a dozen candles from Oswick's shop before I dare write my notes.
finneas_trout.fight_warn: Do not disrupt the curriculum of mirth, scholars, or this heavy volume shall grade your skulls! The syllabus demands a smile from every face in the square!

eleanor_heyling.intro: See how the pages flutter and sing, Chapter Four, Verse Nine of the Great Merriment! Take a ribbon and turn the leaf with me, for sleep is an obsolete footnote tonight!
eleanor_heyling.slip: Where are my spectacles, and why is this papier-mache book glued to my sleeves? Margery will scold me half to death if I have missed the children's supper again.
eleanor_heyling.church_ok: An uncatalogued festivity in the chapel library, you say? Let us go at once and cross-reference their hymns with ours!
eleanor_heyling.church_fail: No, no, the citation clearly places the grand reel right here by the bonfires! Run along, or stay and let the Singing Tome read your palms in rhyme!
eleanor_heyling.calm: My head is ringing like a dropped inkwell, and my heels are blistered raw. Whatever enchantment bound that script to my tongue had no proper bibliography at all.
eleanor_heyling.beaten: A harsh critique, though I cannot fault your methodology given the state I was in. Help me up, please, before Algernon and Sheridan find their aunt sprawled in the confetti.
eleanor_heyling.sheltered: I have read seven treatises on compulsive curses, yet none mentioned the smell of hot mutton pies. Still, this silence is better than any tonic Margery brews for me.
eleanor_heyling.fight_warn: We tolerate no dog-eared sourpusses in our festive edition, my friends! Step into the margins or we shall bind you in red ribbon from cover to cover!

doris_squire.intro: Ring-a-ding, step in line, the law says every foot must rhyme! Shake your cuffs and clang the brass, no sour face is allowed to pass!
doris_squire.slip: Bloody hells, get this copper bucket off my shoulders. If anyone mentions a word of that prancing in my jailhouse, they will pay the fine twice over.
doris_squire.church_ok: A grander peal down at the church, is there? Right then, march in step and keep the chimes ringing!
doris_squire.church_fail: Naught doing, my beat is right here where the ribbons fly and the bells go clang! Move along or join the ring!
doris_squire.calm: My tongue feels thick as boot leather and my ears are ringing foul. A constable ought to keep order, not caper about like a springtime hare.
doris_squire.beaten: Fair clout, that, and I will not book you for assaulting the watch. Just unbuckle this damned bell before my neck gives out.
doris_squire.sheltered: No noise in here, thank the quiet rain and the sunflower's grace. Give me ten minutes on this bench and I will have my notebook straight again.
doris_squire.fight_warn: By order of the Lord of Fools, every frown is a breach of the peace! Dance when the bell rings, or I will clatter your bones to the cobblestones!
doris_squire.tune_intro: Ding-dong, ding-dong, the rhyme comes round and then it drops right on the ground! Help me strike the closing chime, friends, before the measure loses time!
doris_squire.tune_ok: There goes the note, clean and true, like rain upon the meadow rue. My head is clear, and this ridiculous brass harness has lost its grip on me.
doris_squire.tune_fail: No, no, that sours all the brass, and breaks the verse before it can pass! Back to the start of the chime we go!

weston_murdoch.intro: Hark the brass and lift your heels, brothers and sisters, for the carnival chimes wash every heavy heart clean! Come swing in the ring and let your worries peal away!
weston_murdoch.slip: Merciful heavens, my throat is raw and my poor Joan must be frantic. That was no hymn of hope in my mouth, only a hollow jingle that would not let me breathe.
weston_murdoch.church_ok: A chorus of gladness waiting at the church doors, you say? Lead on, friends, and I shall bring the loudest bell in the parish!
weston_murdoch.church_fail: Leave the lanterns when the square is overflowing with song and sweetmeats? Never, friends, come clasp hands and spin until the steeple bows!
weston_murdoch.calm: Praise the dawn that never comes, that clamor has finally let go of my ribs. A man could lose his whole soul inside a smile that wide.
weston_murdoch.beaten: A hard sermon to swallow, friends, though I thank you for sparing my teeth. Help me out of this bell-frame so I can find Joan and the little ones.
weston_murdoch.sheltered: To sit under a quiet vault again feels like cool water on a burn. My father died with a crowd jeering round the oak, and that square out there sounded dreadful close to it.
weston_murdoch.fight_warn: Do not silence the bells of joy, friends, or the chorus will have to chastise you! Every sinner must dance tonight, whether their knees be willing or broken!
weston_murdoch.tune_intro: Ring the high note, ring the low, yet where does the last little cadence go? Lend me your voice, friends, for the final bar keeps slipping from my tongue!
weston_murdoch.tune_ok: Amen and amen, that last chord rang straight through the fog in my skull! Thank you, friends, I am my own man again.
weston_murdoch.tune_fail: Ah, that note rang flat and cold, so the merry carillon must be retold! Once more from the top, with brighter smiles!

holly_aster.intro: Mind the chimney, mind the eaves, my little house dances and never grieves! Take a hot pie from the windowsill and hop with me, one-two-three, thirty-four, never thirty-five!
holly_aster.slip: Oh, my poor ankles, and there is pastry grease all over my apron. Where are Violet and Lavender, did Siv get the girls away from the square?
holly_aster.church_ok: A grander feast laid out down at the quiet church, lovelies? Wait till I tuck my shutters in, and this old cottage will skip right behind you!
holly_aster.church_fail: Go sit in the cold pews when the ovens are roaring and the roofs are kicking up their heels? Stay and dance while we still have nights left to count!
holly_aster.calm: My heart is hammering like a trapped bird, and my hands will not stop shaking. I could feel the floorboards of that costume counting down every step I took.
holly_aster.beaten: Lord above, you have a heavy hand, though it beat spinning until my lungs burst. Help me shed these painted shingles so I can go look for Siv and my girls.
holly_aster.sheltered: Thirty-four candles I have burned, and for an hour out there I thought I would never bake another loaf. Keep the door shut tight, please, until my fingers stop trembling.
holly_aster.fight_warn: Do not knock upon this manor with sour faces, dears, or the rafters will come down on your heads! Eat your sweetmeats and dance, or the house will trample you flat!

thomasin_ardor.intro: Step right up and mind the hem, my friends, for this whole house was stitched to dance! Come spin with me before the velvet roof comes unstuck!
thomasin_ardor.slip: Oh, my knees are trembling like loose basting thread. How long had I been prancing about in this dreadful painted timber and canvas?
thomasin_ardor.church_ok: A quiet gathering with fine new garments to admire sounds simply lovely! Lead the way, and mind my chicken-leg boots on the cobbles!
thomasin_ardor.church_fail: Sit still in a dusty pew when the ribbons are flying so merrily? Never, my dears, this manor has seven more reels to dance!
thomasin_ardor.calm: The music finally stopped pulling at my heels, thank goodness. Whoever stitched this coarse canvas house had no eye for proper seams at all.
thomasin_ardor.beaten: You might have spared the pleated eaves, though I suppose I deserved a sharp tap. At least you knocked this wretched framework off my shoulders.
thomasin_ardor.sheltered: It is mercifully still in here, though my ankles ache from those wooden stilts. I remember smiling while my feet bled, and I could not stop.
thomasin_ardor.fight_warn: Do not tug at the tapestry, friends, or the manor will have to trample you flat! Nobody ruins the grand pattern tonight!

morgan.intro: Buzz and hum, my dears, the hive is overflowing with sweet golden honey tonight! Take a cup and dance around the comb before the swarm drifts away!
morgan.slip: My head feels full of cotton wool and burnt lavender... was I spinning in the square? Thank you for pulling this heavy wicker basket off my shoulders.
morgan.church_ok: A quiet chapel where the bees can rest their wings sounds very sweet indeed! Wait for me, the wicker is a little wide for the lane!
morgan.church_fail: Oh no, the queen says the nectar is only fresh out here by the bonfires! Come back when you want a spoonful of the merry hum!
morgan.calm: The buzzing behind my eyes just faded out like kettle steam... how strange. I was trying to bottle moonbeams for the jester, was I not?
morgan.beaten: Ow... a little arnica salve will mend the bruises, once my hands stop shaking. You hit hard, my friend, though I think nothing milder would have woken me.
morgan.sheltered: It is like waking from one of my old grey spells, except the whole village lost its time together. My pockets are full of sticky festival sweets.
morgan.fight_warn: Please do not kick the hive, my friends, or the stingers will have to come out! Every little bee must defend the Lord of Fools!

baltus_tolliver.intro: Welcome to the sweetest market in the realm, my friends, where every comb is pure gold! Step into the swarm and spend your night with us!
baltus_tolliver.slip: Good grief, they had me trussed up in woven straw like a country hamper. Tell no one you saw me capering, and we shall call this debt settled.
baltus_tolliver.church_ok: An exclusive celebration behind closed doors, away from the rabble? Now that sounds like a profitable venture, so lead on, my enterprising friends!
baltus_tolliver.church_fail: Leave the briskest trade the square has seen all season for a cold stone nave? Not a chance, my friends, the honey is flowing right here!
baltus_tolliver.calm: That infernal piping nearly ruined a very good suit, not to mention my dignity. Whoever rigged this carnival is going to pay a steep tariff.
baltus_tolliver.beaten: You drive a brutal bargain, friend, and my ribs will remember it for a week. Still, I prefer a bruised jaw to wearing a wicker beehive.
baltus_tolliver.sheltered: My pipe is cracked and my ledger is missing, yet I count myself fortunate to be sitting on cold stone. That jester deals in ugly merchandise.
baltus_tolliver.fight_warn: Interfere with the hive's business and you will find our stings remarkably sharp, my friends! Step back and enjoy the music while you still can!

old_rusty.intro: Long legs stride and red ribbons fly, step in the ring where the pie-stacks climb high! Hop with the stork beneath the laughing moon's eye!
old_rusty.slip: Splinters on my shins and feathers in my beard, the broom was forgotten when the painted face leered. Good hands cut the string before the dawn cleared.
old_rusty.church_ok: Stone walls and still air where the bells do not chime? The old bird will follow your steps for a time!
old_rusty.church_fail: No roof for the stork while the fiddles play fast, we hop on the cobbles till the crooked night's past!
old_rusty.calm: The squeaking is gone from the hollow old bone, the stilts clatter down on the Founder's cold stone. A cruel wind it was that left Rusty alone.
old_rusty.beaten: A knock on the noggin to rattle the rhyme, and down tumbles Rusty in ashes and grime. Better a bruise than the jester's bell-chime.
old_rusty.sheltered: Quiet inside where the tall knight keeps guard, while ribbons like blood-streaks blow over the yard. That house on the maypole grins crooked and hard.
old_rusty.fight_warn: Cross not the stork when the carnival calls, or long beaks will peck till the meddler falls! Dance with us nicely inside the bright walls!
old_rusty.letter_charmed: Little bird Bess writes of pots in the hall, wishing her uncle would answer the call! Come sup at the tavern and dance with us all!
old_rusty.letter_free: A scrap of kind ink from a kin-hand so dear, it wets an old cheek though the why isn't clear. Tell little Bess that her uncle is here.

sister_rain.intro: Oh, look how high above the mud we are, blessed and bright as summer birds! Come lift your knees and praise the merry harvest with me!
sister_rain.slip: The Patient Lady preserve us, my calves are rubbed raw by those wicked wooden poles! Even the soil under the cobbles feels sour with this false joy.
sister_rain.church_ok: A sanctuary where the music is gentle as soft rain on the leaves? Oh, take me there at once, my heart is overflowing!
sister_rain.church_fail: Hush your sour mouths, the brightest sun-blessed revel is right here in the square! I will wade through the ribbons till the moon comes down!
sister_rain.calm: That shrill laughter was choking the very roots beneath the Round, and I could only grin along. Pray we mend this bruised earth without more cruelty.
sister_rain.beaten: You struck hard enough to see stars, though I bless your hand for breaking that wicked stupor! Better a split lip than another hour on stilts.
sister_rain.sheltered: Inside these walls I can finally hear my own breath instead of those shrieking pipes. Out there, the ground itself is weeping under the spilled pie.
sister_rain.fight_warn: Do not dare cast a shadow over our joyous feast, you thankless weeds! Smile and step lively, or these long wooden legs will thresh you flat!
